title: 2025-12-03-horizon-alignment-and-resilience-briefing
summary: Quarter-end leadership update focusing on product resilience, hiring reprioritization, cost posture for Dedicated, and a short roadmap reset. CEO framed the conversation around 2026 operating posture and risk margins. Action items include follow-ups on postmortem cadence, a Dedicated capacity pilot review, and org-level hiring freezes for noncritical roles.
transcript:
[00:00:00] Nora Kim: Hey everyone, good afternoon. We're starting the horizon alignment — I know timezone spread, thanks for being here. Quick note, we'll keep to 60 minutes and 10 min Q&A.
[00:00:18] Aaron Reid: Quick housekeeping — recording is on, notes go to the all-hands channel. We'll start with reliability since that's dominating ops and customers.
[00:00:32] Speaker 1 (Liam): On the incident last week, some of the KV cache warm paths failed during a heavy prefix load and that bubbled into higher tail latency. We're still repro'ing the edge case — looks like a memory fragmentation pattern on the custom kernel.
[00:00:50] Aaron Reid: Yes, memory fragmentation and one of our batch pooling heuristics interacted poorly. The fix is staged, and we'll deploy a mitigation tonight (shorter pooling windows). Long term, kernel change + better telemetry.
[00:01:15] Nora Kim: Thanks. This is the kind of thing that impacts renewals. How many customers saw > 2x tail latency?
[00:01:26] Liam Chen: About five enterprise tenants — two on Dedicated, three hosted with specific model variants. No data exfil or integrity issues.
[00:01:40] Sofia Park: From product side we are re-scoping the next two sprints to focus on higher-priority telemetry and a 'fast rollback' path in the console so SEs can toggle routing faster.
[00:02:05] Nora Kim: Good. People question: do we need to hire more infra SREs or can we reassign contractors?
[00:02:16] Maya Patel: Short answer: freeze noncritical roles. Approve two SRE headcount conversions in Q1 and pause three other reqs. We'll circulate the updated hiring matrix.
[00:02:33] Nora Kim: Okay that's the decision for now.
[00:02:40] [00:10:02] Aaron Reid: On Dedicated economics — customers keep asking about predictable unit cost. We have a new proposal to surface quantization and batching profiles in the quote flow so customers can see expected unit cost per 1k tokens. The math is still rough but it'll help sales.
[00:10:28] Sofia Park: Also adding an opt-in 'economics preview' in the Console to show quantization suggestions and expected quality delta versus baseline.
[00:10:45] Nora Kim: Competitors are pushing list pricing, we need a clearer story on what makes Redwood different — predictable SLOs and fallbacks. Bring a one-pager to the next sales sync.
[00:11:05] Liam Chen: Noted.
[00:11:12] [00:20:00] Aaron Reid: A short note on Private/VPC — legal asked for more detail on KMS integrations and audit log retention. We're preparing a package that includes HSM options and a 7-year log retention pattern for regulated customers.
[00:20:25] Nora Kim: Good. Security has to be crisp. We can't leave the SOC 2/ISO threads loose.
[00:20:34] Maya Patel: We'll add an internal owner for compliance artifacts — expect assignment by Friday.
[00:20:42] [00:30:02] Speaker 2 (Finance): On runway and budget — we've adjusted forecast to reflect a more conservative Q1 conversion rate. We're targeting 18 months runway after the changes; if growth re-accelerates we'll revisit.
[00:30:25] Nora Kim: What's the impact on Dedicated capacity investment?
[00:30:36] Speaker 2 (Finance): We'll delay one region expansion into APAC by one quarter; we're keeping the Reserved capacity program but moving the procurement schedule.
[00:30:50] Aaron Reid: That impacts some infra teams — we'll tighten capital spend but keep critical model validation work going.
[00:31:05] [00:40:07] Sofia Park: Roadmap decisions: we're cutting three minor features from the Feb release to protect the Dedicated performance work and the private deployment packaging.
[00:40:20] Nora Kim: Say that again — which features?
[00:40:25] Sofia Park: The multi-model chaining UI, an advanced experimenter flag in Console, and a low-priority analytics export. Those get pushed to Q2.
[00:40:36] Nora Kim: OK prioritize reliability and enterprise packaging.
[00:40:42] [00:50:05] Questions from the floor: 
[00:50:08] Speaker 3 (Eng): Are we expecting increased ticket volume from existing customers as we roll out the mitigation?
[00:50:15] Liam Chen: Probably a bump for seven to ten days. SE and Support will spool up triage templates.
[00:50:25] Speaker 4 (PM): Will the hiring freeze affect product contractors?
[00:50:30] Maya Patel: We'll assess criticality per role — product contractors for the Dedicated effort are greenlighted. Noncritical research contractors paused.
[00:50:42] [01:00:00] Nora Kim: Final framing — this is a deliberate move to tighten operations and protect our enterprise stories. We cannot scale without reliability. We will be transparent with customers and partners.
[01:00:15] Aaron Reid: Quick ask: SEs, please gather three benchmark prompts that reproduce tail latency for your top customers; send to infra@redwood by EOD Monday.
[01:00:30] Sofia Park: Product will share the trimmed roadmap and a one-pager for sales.
[01:00:40] Maya Patel: People team will publish the hiring matrix and a FAQ for managers.
[01:01:10] Nora Kim: Thanks everyone. We'll follow up with a short postmortem and the next check-in in two weeks.
[01:01:20] [END]
next_steps: Infra mitigation deploy scheduled tonight - update in ops channel
Postmortem draft to be circulated by infra lead by Friday
Hiring matrix and pause list by People team by Thursday
Dedicated economics one-pager for sales by Product before next sales sync
Compliance package (KMS/HSM + audit retention) assignment by Friday

Maya Patel: publish hiring matrix & manager FAQ (due 2025-12-04)
